title: Everdisplay's revenues drop 20% in Q3 2026, as demand for its AMOLED products remain weak
content: Everdisplay (EDO) announced its financial results for Q3 2026. Revenues in the quarter were $159 million, down 19.8% from Q3 2025, and the company posted a net loss of $74 million. In the first three quarters of 2026, EDO's revenues reached $545 million (down 8.6% from the same period in 2025), with a net loss of $207 million ($213 million after deducting non-recurring items).

title: More details emerge on LG Display's and Hanwha Systems' fighter jet OLED project, as Boeing asks to adopt OLEDs in its F-15 jets
content: Last month we reported that Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources is planning an R&D project with LG Display and Hanwha Systems to develop AMOLED displays for fighter jet cockpits. Now Korea's THE ELEC provides more details on this project - and it says that Boeing has asked Hanwha Systems to replace the LCDs in its fighter jets with OLED displays.

title: Namuga expands beyond Samsung with humanoid robot camera modules
content: South Korean image-sensing module maker Namuga is accelerating its physical AI strategy after securing a supply deal with a global humanoid robot company. The company is preparing for shipments and mass production while targeting revenue of KRW1 trillion (approximately US$754.7 million) by 2030.

title: Texas Instruments sees up to $1,000 in chip content per humanoid robot as analog supply tightens
content: Texas Instruments (TI) held its latest earnings call this week, projecting fourth-quarter 2026 revenue of US$5.8 billion to US$6.3 billion. The midpoint of its guidance is broadly in line with third-quarter revenue, outperforming the seasonal declines typically seen in the fourth quarter.

title: Magnate Technology sees aerospace, semiconductor growth opportunities
content: Magnate Technology expects rising aircraft engine demand and semiconductor equipment opportunities to support growth as it expands production capacity, with implications for global aviation and chip supply chains. The aerospace components maker forecasts revenue of nearly NT$2 billion (US$61.5 million) in 2026 and expects 15% to 20% revenue growth in 2027.

title: Panasonic Avionics sold over 500,000 Astrova 4K OLED in-flight entertainment screens, expands its production capacity sixfold
content: Panasonic Avionics announced that it has sold 500,000 of its Astrova 4K OLED in-flight entertainment (IFE) screens. Since its launch in 2022, Astrova has been selected by more than 45 airlines across more than 150 aircraft installation programs, and Panasonic says that it is the fastest-adopted IFE solution in the company's history.
